 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma
 Order

The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973("Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 239/2015 registered at Police Station Jahangirpuri, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all other proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Dalveer Kaur and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Rajesh Kumar from Police Station Jahangirpuri, Delhi.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 21.01.2014.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is stated that due to temperamental differences, parties started residing separately since 21.06.2014.

It is stated that respondent no. 2 had filed a complaint before CAW cell upon which an FIR bearing no. 239/2015 for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 IPC was registered at Police Station Jahangirpuri, Delhi against petitioners.

During the pendency of the present case, with the intervention of relatives and well wishers, parties had mutually agreed to dissolve their marriage before the learned Principal Judge, Family Courts, North District, Rohini, Delhi.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family member.

6. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received last instalment of Rs.
50,000/- today, i.e., 17.04.2023 and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

7. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

8. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 239/2015 registered at Police Station Jahangirpuri, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
9. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
10. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J APRIL 19, 2023/
